title: Configuration Resolution and Runtime Behavior
readerIntent: Understand how configuration becomes effective and how runtime changes remain governed.
summary: Nodics loads selected module configuration in deterministic order, merges eligible layered values, validates contracts, and starts services only after their required context is available.

sections.heading: Startup sequence
items: Resolve the selected environment and server or node topology.
Discover module groups and modules belonging to that topology.
Load framework defaults before more specific project and deployment layers.
Merge supported objects using the framework configuration contract.
Initialize classes, schemas, services, routes, pipelines, events, and module lifecycle hooks.
Declare readiness only when required startup work has completed; optional integrations recover asynchronously according to their resilience policy.

sections.heading: Scope and precedence
paragraphs: A more specific layer may refine a supported value while the reusable module remains authoritative for its default and contract. Environment, server, node, tenant, and customer scope are distinct concerns; the effective value must be explainable from the selected runtime context.

sections.heading: Canonical identity and topology selection
paragraphs: A server name may appear in several environments. Runtime resolution combines the chosen environment and server; node resolution additionally uses its server. Short names remain usable without losing unambiguous runtime identity.
An interactive terminal may ask for an environment when the server name is ambiguous. Automation must provide explicit coordinates and must never select the first match silently.

sections.heading: Merge behavior
items: Defaults load before more specific eligible layers.
Owned object namespaces merge only according to the framework configuration contract.
Arrays, primitives, maps, and nested objects retain their documented merge or replacement semantics.
An override cannot change the ownership or type of a contract merely because it loads later.
The effective configuration remains inspectable for authorized diagnostics.

sections.heading: Startup readiness and resilience
paragraphs: Required configuration and dependencies complete before the capability reports ready. Optional coordination, such as registering a running module with BackOffice, may retry asynchronously when it does not determine local correctness.

This keeps latency-sensitive startup and recovery paths bounded while ensuring optional discovery eventually converges. Retry, backoff, idempotency, health, and shutdown behavior are part of the lifecycle contract.

sections.heading: Governed runtime changes
items: Preview validates shape, policy, dependencies, and impact without activation.
Approval records the intended change and authorized decision.
Activation applies only a supported runtime configuration contract.
Audit retains previous and next snapshots and actor context.
Rollback restores a known prior state through the same governed boundary.

sections.heading: Runtime-change failure behavior
items: Preview rejection leaves the current configuration untouched.
Approval does not activate a change by itself unless the contract explicitly combines those actions.
Activation failure preserves or restores the last known valid state.
Partially applied provider changes require rollback or a clearly reported degraded state.
Concurrent updates use version or conflict controls instead of last-writer ambiguity.
Audit records safe before-and-after evidence without exposing secrets.

sections.heading: Example resolution
paragraphs: The cache capability defines a default lifetime. A project retains that default, startioLocal shortens it for development, and monoServer adds no further override. The effective value is therefore explained by the environment layer.

If an approved runtime contract later changes an eligible tenant lifetime, that value applies only in its resolved tenant scope. Restarting or rolling back follows the cache contract; another tenant and another environment remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Operational evidence
items: Selected project, environment, server, node, and active modules.
Configuration source and effective value without secret disclosure.
Validation, readiness, retry, activation, rollback, and conflict signals.
Correlation between a governed request, approval, actor, version, and runtime result.
Focused tests for restart, dependency loss, repeated registration, invalid configuration, and recovery.
